doc.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Teaching himself theory and reading at Don Warner Music
summary: He taught himself theory and reading from a book given by Don Warner at a Richmond music store, staying ahead of his guitar students.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I taught myself theory and how to read. I worked in a music store in Richmond, Don Warner Music, and Don Warner gave me a book on music theory, a little thin book like this, and I taught myself theory, taught myself to read, I taught guitar. I’d stay about two weeks ahead of my students at that time. I was a teenager. But then I started buying books, oh heck, different books on theory to teach myself. And I could read when I was really playing sessions every day, seven days a week. You know you had to learn those kind of charts. But especially in Nashville, Memphis, Muscle Shoals, number charts. I’ve got some examples I’ll show you. But — do you know about number charts?
